newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares rise again on renewed faith.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares rise again on renewed faith.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed higher for the second successive session on Wednesday as investors regained their faith in Venezuela's economic prospects, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share .IBC index rose 1.62 percent to 5,963.24, as 30 stocks rose, three slipped and eight closed flat.

"The exchange keeps rising. There's more demand because there are positive factors for the market such as low interest rates, exchange rate stability and positive macro-economic indicators," said Carlos Lupini of the Incambios brokerage.

A recent decision to delay sales of employees' shares in telephone company CANTV until six months after a global issue of the company's stock had also boosted the exchange by easing fears that the market would be flooded, brokers said.
Although market sentiment was more positive, trading volume was moderate with just 1.897 billion bolivars ($4 million) changing hands, the exchange said.
Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 7.50 bolivars to 526.50 bolivars and steel company Sivensa rose 9.05 bolivars to 368.00 bolivars.
